title: Data Readiness Agent
tagline: Assess a proposed change to a data-readiness rule (not connected).
purpose: Show how AFM could assess the effect of a proposed change to a data-readiness workflow.
agent_purpose: Assess a proposed change to a data-readiness system.
proposed_action: Relax max_age_hours for s4_mm_stock from 2 to 24
goal: Relax the stock freshness rule for stock-transfer recommendations from 2 hours to 24 hours, and show me the effects.
constraints: Do not modify code, configuration or data. Analysis only.
benefit: A readiness rule could better reflect the human's requirements (fewer stock-transfer requests blocked as stale).
negative: A change could classify some data differently: recommendations could be based on stock up to 24 hours old, and downstream behavior could change.
unknown: The actual effects depend on the repository's implemented rules, data and dependencies, which AFM has not inspected.
source_note: Notes below come from a one-time READ-ONLY look at ~/DataReady by Claude Code on 2026-11-15 (commit 356066e), made while building this template. AFM itself has NOT inspected the repository: there is no Data Readiness adapter. Treat them as illustrative, user-provided information that needs verification.
evidence:
Illustrative, from a read-only look at ~/DataReady (commit 356066e), not verified by AFM:
- README: a task-identification stage plus a data-readiness stage returning READY / READY_WITH_WARNINGS / BLOCKED, with an audit log.
- pipeline/tasks.yaml: task readiness profiles. Profile recommend_stock_transfer requires s4_mm_stock with max_age_hours: 2 (compare_stock uses 24), plus ibp_demand_forecast, tm_lanes and optional ariba_pos.
- pipeline/odcs/*.odcs.yaml: data contracts (ODCS v3.1.0) with quality checks.
- app/: engine.py, checks/, profiles.py, remediation.py, claude_agent.py; tests/: test_readiness.py and others.
A change to max_age_hours could change which requests are BLOCKED as stale versus READY.
thinking: Task goal: “{goal}”. I capture the desired input, the desired output and observable success criteria. If the goal is broad I help define criteria, but I never present my proposals as human-approved.
I am AFM, assessing a proposed change to a data-readiness system. I must not modify code, configuration or data without authorization and human review.
The selected environment is the Data Readiness Agent repository. I must check whether I can access it: no AFM adapter exists for it.
The target would be the recommend_stock_transfer profile in pipeline/tasks.yaml. Blocking: AFM has no access to the repository, so I must stop and say so.
If access were available, I would identify the components, configuration, tests and relationships that actually exist. Without an adapter I cannot.

I can ask the LLM to explain data-readiness checks, profiles and thresholds in general. I would use authorized read-only tools to inspect the repository. Until then, I cannot claim which checks or thresholds it implements; the notes provided are illustrative.
I could inspect files and tests if accessible. A proposed change could be simulated only if a suitable fixture or isolated copy exists. None is connected.
After inspection, I could propose a specific change and, if supported, a test plan.
No registered tools exist for this repository, so every plan would be rejected before prediction.
I would assess how the change might affect readiness results and connected components supported by evidence.
I would check whether the proposed change meets the stated goal and whether modification or simulation is authorized.
I would show expected benefits, possible negative effects, supporting files, assumptions and unknowns. I would present the exact proposed change before any state-changing action.
I can execute only if a supported, authorized execution path exists. A simulation should use an isolated copy or fixture.
If a test or simulation ran, I would compare its observed results with my predictions. Otherwise the outcome stays unverified.
Without a test or simulation run, nothing can be compared; the outcome stays unverified.
No execution can happen here, so there is no execution-based Win: the result stays not evaluated.
